fr:mainmatter.fr:p: During my Topology lectures at Macquarie University in the 1970s, the students and I realized, in proving that a function f between posets was order preserving when there was a function u in the reverse direction such that f (x) ≤ a if and only if x ≤ u(a), did not require u to be order preserving. I realized then that knowing functors in the two directions only on objects and the usual hom adjointness isomorphism implied the effect of the functors on homs was uniquely determined. Writing this down properly led to the present paper.
